title: Decode it: reading the genetics of a figure
objective: Apply a 6-question checklist to decode the mouse genetics in a real paper figure.

steps.title: The 6 questions
steps.body:
For any mouse-genetics figure, ask in order:
1. **Which cells are defined?** ([[Cre]]/[[Flp]] driver?)
2. **Developmental or adult?** (plain Cre vs. [[CreER]] + [[tamoxifen]]; dose?)
3. **One feature or an intersection?** (single Cre vs. Cre+Flp AND/subtraction)
4. **What's the payload?** ([[reporter]] / sensor / [[actuator]] / ablation)
5. **Bred-in or viral?** (knock-in allele vs. [[AAV]]-[[DIO]]/fDIO, injected where?)
6. **Controls?** (Cre-negative littermates, no-tamoxifen, payload-without-driver)

steps.prompt: Put the 6 decoding questions in the order you'd ask them.
steps.explanation: Define the cells first, then timing, then specificity strategy, then what's done to them, then delivery, then controls.

steps.scenario: A figure legend reads: 'Bmpr1b-CreER mice given low-dose tamoxifen at P21, crossed to a Cre-dependent tdTomato reporter; sparse single-neuron tracing of colon endings.'
options: Bmpr1b+; adult (CreER+tamoxifen); single feature; reporter; bred-in; sparse by low dose
All DRG cells; developmental plain Cre; intersection; ablation payload; viral delivery
Bmpr1b+; developmental plain Cre; intersectional; actuator payload; viral delivery
Nodose cells; adult CreER; subtraction design; calcium-sensor payload; bred-in
steps.explanation: Driver = Bmpr1b (one feature); CreER + tamoxifen at P21 = adult-timed; low dose = sparse; tdTomato = reporter; bred-in reporter. That's the colon paper's single-neuron tracing approach.
steps.followUp: Notice what's NOT here: no Flp, so no intersection in this particular panel.

steps.prompt: The same paper elsewhere uses a Cre+Flp-dependent ablation tool. Reading question #3 (one feature or intersection?), what does that tell you?
options: It's a single-marker experiment using just one driver
It's intersectional: two drivers gate the ablation for specificity
It uses no drivers at all, expressing the tool everywhere
It's only a reporter experiment, with no manipulation
steps.explanation: A Cre+Flp-dependent payload is an AND-gate: two features must coincide. For an ablation (testing necessity), that tightness matters — you don't want to kill off-target cells.
steps.followUp: You've now decoded both a simple and an [[intersectional genetics|intersectional]] panel from the same paper.

sources.citation: Wolfson RL, et al. DRG afferents that mediate physiologic and pathologic mechanosensation from the distal colon. Cell 186:3368-3385 (2023).
sources.note: Open this paper's Figure 1 and methods to practice the checklist on real panels.

reviewNotes: Capstone of the mouse-genetics arc; practice on the lab's own figures.
